# Context Fence

> Stops AI agents leaking secrets. A local MCP policy proxy for AI coding agents: schema-based tool call checks under 10ms, secret stripping, and an append-only local audit log. Zero cloud routing. A product of Synthrun.

Context Fence sits between an AI coding agent and the tools it calls. Every tool call is checked against local YAML policy rules before it executes — destructiveness, filesystem scope, destination domains, secret-shaped values, and prompt-injection payloads in tool output. Blocked calls are logged locally with the reason. The proxy is free, runs fully on the user's machine, and routes nothing anywhere. Current release v1.1.9-b (macOS universal dmg, Windows installer, Linux AppImage/deb/rpm).

## FAQ

- Does agent data leave the machine? No — the proxy runs locally and every policy check happens locally.
- How fast is the policy check? Under 10ms per call — a schema match against local YAML rules, not an LLM judge.
- What does it block? Destructive calls, filesystem escape, non-allowlisted domains, secret leakage, and prompt-injection payloads.
- How is it different from MintMCP, Lasso, or Kong AI Gateway? They inspect agent traffic in their cloud; Context Fence inspects on the user's machine and routes nothing.
- Is it free? The local proxy is free and is the core product. The hosted control plane (policy sync + audit aggregation only) is planned and not built yet.
